title: Valid proofs & surviving arguments
review_basis: Mathematical review of the current canonical Markdown and focused proof notes. The 14 core rows below represent the earlier collected arguments. The cubic attraction result and asymptotic comparison are listed separately as later additions.
audit_scope: Compared the complete 16-page electric-orange PDF, the 17-page illustrated PDF, their canonical Markdown and JSON, visible page renders and extracted text. The reported page numbers match the 16-page edition. The exact file or excerpt supplied to the earlier reviewer is unknown.
audit_summary: The inspected source and printed notation already contain the correct formulas. Nested powers and derivatives can lose meaning during PDF text extraction. The revision improves readable mathematical text and separates the established arguments from later additions.

statements.title: Logistic two-cycle
statements.domain: Real r > 3; additionally r ≤ 4 for the conventional invariant interval [0,1].
statements.statement: The second-iterate factorization gives two distinct nontrivial cycle points x₊ and x₋, exchanged by fᵣ. Their derivatives multiply to μ(r) = 4 + 2r − r².
statements.qualification: The factorization, exchange identities and derivative formulas follow by polynomial algebra.

statements.title: Paired quarter-turn matrix
statements.statement: At μ(r*) = −1, C² = −I and C⁴ = I. Rescaling by S = diag(√a, 1/√a), a = √2 − 1, gives S⁻¹CS = [[0,1], [−1,0]].
statements.qualification: C is the explicitly defined paired linear matrix. It has determinant 1 and rank 2; it is not Euclidean orthogonal in the original coordinates.

statements.title: Vanishing derivative of the return displacement
statements.domain: At either point p₊ or p₋ of the r* = 1 + √6 two-cycle.
statements.statement: The second-return derivative is −1, the fourth-return derivative is 1, and the derivative of f⁴ − id is zero at each cycle point.
statements.qualification: These are local derivative identities. The critical point is a separate point: fᵣ′(1/2) = 0 and fᵣ(1/2) = r/4.

statements.title: Zero cycle Lyapunov exponent
statements.domain: The exact two-cycle at r* = 1 + √6; exponent per original logistic update.
statements.statement: The cycle Lyapunov exponent equals one half of log |d₊d₋| and is exactly zero.
statements.qualification: The zero exponent alone leaves nonlinear stability undecided. The separate later cubic argument establishes local attraction.

statements.title: Two constructions of six
statements.domain: Tadd(y) = frac(2·3ʸ), Tmul(y) = frac(6ʸ), y ∈ [0,1), N ≥ 1; orbit segments with the stated branch derivatives.
statements.statement: Each finite-time average uses exactly N terms, indexed 0 through N−1. The branch log derivatives are affine functions of y, so their averages and difference are exact functions of the respective orbit means.
statements.qualification: Ordinary derivatives fail at fraction-part jumps; the source states the branch and endpoint conventions. Infinite-time formulas require the orbit means to converge. No common invariant measure is assumed.

statements.title: Dimension and cardinality
statements.domain: Finite-dimensional vector spaces over the indicated scalar fields; cardinality of their underlying sets.
statements.statement: R³ × R² has real dimension 5; R³ ⊗R R² has real dimension 6; C³ has real dimension 6 and complex dimension 3. All three underlying sets have cardinality 2^ℵ₀.
statements.latex: \dim_{\mathbb R}(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^2)=5,\quad\dim_{\mathbb R}(\mathbb R^3\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb R^2)=6,\quad|\mathbb R^5|=|\mathbb R^6|=|\mathbb C^3|=2^{\aleph_0}.
statements.qualification: The product, tensor product, scalar field and set cardinality specify different mathematical questions.

statements.title: Cubic factorization and odd-step conventions
statements.domain: Complex z; odd positive integer n for the iteration conventions.
statements.statement: z³ − 1 = (z − 1)(z² + z + 1). The expressions 3n + 1 and (3n + 1)/2 denote distinct odd-step conventions; the latter includes one division by two.
statements.qualification: The full odd-to-odd step removes all factors of two. A connection from these formulas to the logistic matrix still needs an explicit map. T₀–T₃ remain undefined archival labels.

statements.title: Exact reduction of Z(p)
statements.domain: Odd integers p ≥ 3; primality is not required.
statements.statement: Euler’s even-zeta evaluation gives Z(p) = 1 + exp(cₚπᵖ) with positive rational cₚ = 2^(p−2)|Bₚ₋₁|/p!. The signed Bernoulli formula gives the same coefficient.
statements.qualification: Lowercase c denotes the same coefficient throughout. The p = 2 definition encounters the pole at ζ(1).

statements.title: Conditional algebraic independence
statements.domain: Assume full complex Schanuel; p₁,…,pₖ are pairwise distinct odd integers ≥ 3.
statements.statement: The tuple π, Z(p₁), …, Z(pₖ) is algebraically independent over Q. Apply Schanuel to iπ and the real inputs cₚⱼπᵖⱼ, then compare transcendence degrees by field containment.
statements.qualification: The imaginary part isolates iπ in a rational linear relation; transcendence of π handles the distinct real powers. Adjoining i is algebraic. This proof uses the complex form of the assumption.

statements.title: Dyadic series and vanishing remainder
statements.domain: f(x) = Σₙ≥₀ x^(2^n), |x| < 1; xₖ = exp(−2^(−k)), integer k ≥ 0.
statements.statement: The functional equation f(x) = x + f(x²) gives f(xₖ) = k + C + Rₖ. The explicit tail satisfies 2^(−k) − 4^(−k)/6 ≤ Rₖ ≤ 2^(−k).
statements.qualification: Absolute convergence, an index shift and t − t²/2 ≤ 1 − e^(−t) ≤ t give the proof. The constant belongs to this specified dyadic path.

statements.title: Ordinary palindrome count
statements.domain: Independent uniform symbols; alphabet size integer q ≥ 2; string length integer n ≥ 1.
statements.statement: There are q^ceil(n/2) palindromes among qⁿ strings, so the probability is q^(−floor(n/2)). The q = 4, n = 40 example is exactly 2^(−40).
statements.qualification: The formula includes odd lengths. For reverse complementation with a fixed-point-free complement pairing, odd lengths are impossible and even lengths have probability q^(−n/2).

statements.title: Global convergence of the alternating towers
statements.domain: Real c > 1, L = log c; v₀ ≥ 1; u = c^(−v), v = cᵘ.
statements.statement: F_L(v) = exp(L exp(−Lv)) maps [1,∞) into I = [1, exp(1/e)] and is a contraction there with uniform bound q = 4 exp(1/e − 2) < 1. The solution is unique and every stated initial value converges.
statements.qualification: Banach’s theorem proves convergence and uniqueness for this explicitly defined alternating-sign system. The residual estimate is an exact-arithmetic statement.

statements.title: Sharp height and number of bases
statements.statement: The maximum upper phase is vmax = exp(W₀(1/e)), attained at cpeak = exp(1/vmax). Every height strictly between 1 and vmax has exactly two finite bases; vmax has one, and heights above vmax or equal to 1 have none.
statements.latex: v\log v=t e^{-t}\le1/e,\quad t=v\log c,\quad v_{\max}=e^{W_0(1/e)}.
statements.qualification: Strict increase of v log v and the two branches of t exp(−t) give the complete classification. cpeak names the maximizing base, not a maximum allowed base.

statements.title: Finite prime-polynomial counting
statements.domain: P_X(z) = Σprime p≤X zᵖ, integer X ≥ 2; integer N ≥ 4; formal finite coefficient extraction.
statements.statement: [zᴺ]P_N(z)² counts ordered prime pairs summing to N. Adding the diagonal indicator and dividing by two counts unordered pairs. [z²]P_(X+2)(z)P_X(z⁻¹) counts prime pairs p,p+2 with p ≤ X.
statements.qualification: D(N) = 1 exactly when N/2 is an integer prime. These are direct coefficient identities; the full argument is present in its standalone note.

supplements.title: Later addition: the surviving logistic cubic
supplements.domain: r* = 1 + √6; either cycle phase p±; H = f⁴; sufficiently small real h.
supplements.statement: H(p±+h) − (p±+h) = −K±h³ + O(h⁴), with K± = 20r*²(2 ± √2) > 0. The displacement has a zero of exactly order three.
supplements.qualification: This later derivation is separate from the earlier collected-proof review. The exact quartic coefficients and composed cubic were independently checked symbolically.

supplements.title: Later addition: local attraction and its rate
supplements.domain: g(h) = H(p±+h) − p±; sufficiently small nonzero real initial h₀.
supplements.statement: The iterates preserve the sign of h, decrease in absolute value and converge to zero. If hₙ = gⁿ(h₀), then n hₙ² → 1/(2K±).
supplements.qualification: This supplies the nonlinear stability argument. One n-step equals four original logistic updates; the conclusion is local.

supplements.title: Later addition: a shared leading decay scale
supplements.domain: Rₖ from the dyadic note; integer k > 1 tending to infinity.
supplements.qualification: The dyadic bound and a separate zeta-tail estimate prove an asymptotic comparison. It does not define a shared dynamical system.

supplements.title: Defined geometric model for the next connection
supplements.domain: X = S¹ × (−δ,δ), Φ(θ,h) = (θ+ω mod 2π, g(h)), with δ from the local attraction proof.
supplements.statement: The invariant circle S¹ × {0} attracts transversely, with distance |gⁿ(h)| tending to zero while the angular coordinate follows its prescribed rotation.
supplements.qualification: This explicitly defined model has a proved attraction property. A physical brane interpretation and a full logistic–Hopf conjugacy remain separate open questions.
